independent_graph_checks: All 41760 queries: separately constructed raw/closed explicit multigraphs, DFS ranking reachability, Floyd feasibility and edgewise BF potential/negative-cycle certificates for both representations.
source_validation_replay: Fresh copied original source built with existing Zig; validate only; both validation and expected_batches outputs byte-identical.
reporting_correction: Existing RESULTS omits explicit tie counts: all720 Q192 quartet versus cheap is 3 faster / 5 slower / 1 tie across nine paired blocks. Original files preserved.

cheap flags for cheap and quartet

query graph construction and BF/route decision work

measurement_boundary.capacity_reuse: One Scratch persists across all jobs; vector capacity is reused after common warmup. Graph weights, BF labels and predecessors are rewritten whenever BF is called. No fresh scratch allocation is promised per job.
measurement_boundary.normalization: Each elapsed interval is divided by repeats*plans_in_stratum; summary values are medians/min/max of nine block-average ns/job observations. Per-query equivalents are further divided by Q, not separately timed query latencies.

limitations: One Windows CPU and one specified implementation; no affinity/frequency isolation or confidence intervals.
Recorded manifest hashes bind saved source/input/order/results; files alone cannot independently establish trusted wall-clock predeclaration chronology.
The original timed executable hash is bound by PRE_TIMING_AUDIT, but this audit did not observe the past timing process.
Q192 repeats the same 48 frozen queries four times and adds no independent workloads.
Each scaling stratum has only three fixed plans; timing repeats and nine blocks are repeated observations, not additional workloads.
Quartet classification may stop on its first obstruction and is bypassed on cheap-exact plans. These observed costs do not establish universal O(n^4) cost behavior or optimality.
Storage depends on representation: positions/edges are copied per job, dense closure and closure pairs may be quadratic, scratch weights signed128 are quadratic; rectangles/queries are preloaded.
No GPU/native measurement, H20 outward-auditor timing, full certificate-serving latency or application speedup follows.
Strata occur in ascending order per block; Q and route orders are shuffled, but stratum/time effects are not independently randomized.
Normalized values are block averages across plans, not a distribution of individually timed job or query requests.
CPU/OS identity and historical controls are run metadata; this audit did not observe host controls during the earlier run.
